name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 1, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor MacLean at
5:00 p.m., on February 1, 2010 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 27, 1010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma (arrived at 5:03 p.m.)
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor MacLean
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:10 p.m.)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

City Council Minutes  1  February 1, 2010
 CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One Matter of Pending Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is Oso Viejo
  Neighbors Association v. City of Mission Viejo et al. Case Number 30-2009-
  00319861.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor MacLean declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that Closed Session Item CS1 was not completed and the
Council will return to closed session after the open session business is finished. Item 7 on the
Agenda will be publicly addressed after the second closed session is completed this evening.

Mr. Curley further announced that for item CS2, the Council provided direction to staff but there
was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize 2009 Employees of the Year

  Mayor MacLean present plaques of appreciation to (1) Library Manager Stephanie
  Tanton, City of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; (2) Deputy Jay Christian, Orange
  County Sheriff’s Department Employee of the Year; and (3) Fire Captain Jack Perisho,
  Orange County Fire Authority Employee of the Year.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Sharon Cody, M.V.: expressed concern that Council candidate Dale Tyler has broken a number
of laws and she encouraged residents to vote no on the recall.

Larry Maurer, M.V.: stated that he is worried that many of the great things residents have come
to enjoy and expect in Mission Viejo may change after tomorrow’s election.

Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: stated that Lance MacLean has done nothing against the City and the
dirty tactics of the recall proponents have no place in Mission Viejo.

Jim Holmes, M.V.: encouraged residents to vote no on the recall.

Chuck VanArman, M.V.: stated that he hopes that the City Manager’s contract is not approved in
a hurry prior to the election tomorrow.

City Council Minutes  2  February 1, 2010
 Neil Lonsinger, M.V.: stated that he is in favor of a dog park but the studies on location and cost
need to continue.

Eileen Lynch, M.V.: stated that she has been shocked at the rude, immature behavior from
members of the audience and from a Council Member at the dais. She urged everyone to set
aside personal vendettas, vote no on the recall and yes for Dave Leckness.

Hugh Armstrong, M.V.: stated that he feels very fortunate to live in Mission Viejo and he is
disappointed that the recall election has caused so much discord in the City. He advocates a no
vote on the recall and yes for candidate Dave Leckness.

Daniel Avery, M.V.: requested that the City Council make a finding of urgency and vote to file a
lawsuit against the recall committee’s organizers and members, the Tyler campaign organizers,
Council Members Schlicht and Ledesma and resident Larry Gilbert.

Eric Chastain, M.V.: stated that the recall is a big waste of money and time. He encouraged
residents to vote no on the recall and yes for Dave Leckness.

Diane Nill, M.V.: apologized to Mayor MacLean for signing the recall petition and stated that
she did so before she had all the facts. Stated that the recall effort has been full of lies and
distortions and we have far more to be thankful for than we have to complain about.

Tom Ross, M.V.: stated that the Mayor and Council have done a good job and he is really angry
that the City is required to pay $270,000 for the recall. He encouraged residents to vote no on
the recall and yes for Dave Leckness.

Sherri Butterfield, M.V.: requested that the Council, on behalf of its residents, file a lawsuit
against the committee that circulated the recall petitions, against the committee that is seeking to
elect Dale Tyler, and against the thirty four persons who signed the notice of intention to recall
Mr. MacLean.

Larry Ryan, M.V.: encouraged the Council to pursue full recovery of the money spent on the
recall. He encouraged residents to vote their hearts and vote for Dave Leckness.

Robert Bruchmann, M.V.: stated that the dishonesty in this recall debate has become the norm,
not an exception. He encouraged residents to vote no on the recall and yes for Dave Leckness.

David Allen, M.V.: asked voters to be aware and informed of the candidates involved in the
recall. He stated that his vote will be in support of the current City Council, staff, police and
everything that’s great about Mission Viejo.

Wendy Bucknam, M.V.: applauded the City Council for paying attention to the kids in the
community. She stated that we are all tired of the negativity from the people who have put forth
this recall and the sleeping giant has awoken.

City Council Minutes  3  February 1, 2010
 John Maginnis, M.V.: criticized candidate Dale Tyler for attacking the Girl Scouts on the City
blog yet he is someone who has apparently broken State laws. He encouraged residents to vote
no on the recall and yes for Dave Leckness.

Helen Workun, M.V.: requested that candidate Dale Tyler withdraw his bid for City Council.

Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: urged residents to go to the polls tomorrow and vote no on the recall. She
announced that there will be a car pool service for those who cannot drive to the polls and ride
requests can be made by calling 837-5484. Ms. Boyce also reminded residents of the free flu
and H1N1 vaccine clinic at the Community Center on February 10 from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.

Rich Heimann, M.V.: stated that it is unconscionable that a brigade of naysayers would take an
issue so far as to cost the City $270,000 for the recall election and then promote a candidate who
is damaged goods.

Rick Sandzimier, M.V.: stated that he has been discouraged and disappointed in the community
at recent Council meetings but tonight he is very proud as he watches residents band together.
He thanked Lance MacLean for his service to the community and stated that he hopes the recall
will be defeated.

Nancy Cho, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Board of Directors for the South Orange County
Regional Chamber of Commerce, she stated that the Chamber opposes the recall and supports
candidate Dave Leckness.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 6 and 7 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

City Council Minutes  4  February 1, 2010
   Approved the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of January 18, 2010, as presented.

3.  Summary of FY 2009-10 Budget Amendments To Date

  Received and filed.

4.  Check Register dated January 8, 2010, in the amount of $674,713.35

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated January 15, 2010, in the amount of $2,043,015.02

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  Bleacher Shade Covers

  Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Council Member Ledesma inquired about the incorrect numbers in the bid and asked
  which number was mathematically correct.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1) reject
  all bids for the construction of sixteen (16) bleacher shade covers at Marty Russo Youth
  Athletic Park, Beebe Park, Curtis Park, and Gilleran Park baseball fields and authorize
  staff to re-bid; and (2) adopt Resolution 10-04 Creating Capital Improvement Project
  #321 and Amending the FY 09-10 Budget to Include Funding for the Construction of
  Sixteen (16) Bleacher Shade Covers in the Amount of $141,000.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  5  February 1, 2010
 7.  Sixth Amendment to City Manager Employment Agreement

  The following expressed opposition to the proposed amendments in the agreement: Larry
  Gilbert, M.V.; Barbara Anderson, M.V.; and Neil Lonsinger, M.V.

  This item was continued until after the Closed Session.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Dennis Wilberg drew the Council's attention to the 2009 Annual Report which is
now available on the City's web site and will be delivered to residents’ homes later this week.

City Attorney’s Report

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

8.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

9.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ury announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the
  Foothill/Eastern TCA.

10.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

11.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Ledesma

Reminded residents to vote in tomorrow's election.

City Council Minutes  6  February 1, 2010
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht reminded voters to ask themselves why the Sheriff's Association
Union and the Apartment Association have spent $120,000 in special interest money on the
recall election. She discussed her request for a Deputy Sheriff to be on duty in the Council
Chamber until Mayor MacLean leaves because she feels uncomfortable with his behavior. She
stated that Lance MacLean needs to be removed from office and that’s why she is involved in the
recall. Council Member Schlicht asked residents to vote their conscience in the election
tomorrow.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury agreed that residents need to get out and exercise their civic duty by voting
in tomorrow's election. He expressed concern with the rationalizations by a small group of
people who have removed all sense of ethics to get the results that they want. Council Member
Ury stated that it is difficult to try to do what is good for the City with the distraction and
annoyance of this election and the improper activities of candidate Dale Tyler. He stated that the
main proponents have totally detached their sense of ethics and right-doing under the guise of the
recall and regardless of the outcome of the election, everyone at the dais will be just fine. He
stated that he is looking forward to the election so the City can move forward and he reminded
residents to get out and vote.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that she was pleased that the meeting started on such a positive
note when the Council honored and recognized three of our valued City employees. She
congratulated Stephanie Tanton, Captain Jack Perisho, and Deputy Jay Christian and stated that
we are so blessed to have this caliber of employees working on the Mission Viejo team. She also
congratulated Mission Viejo's High School football coach, Bob Johnson, who has just been
recognized as the NFL High School Coach of the Year. She expressed her pride in Coach
Johnson and the Mission Viejo Diablos team and thanked them for the way they represent the
City. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley discussed the recently published 2009 Annual Report and she
highlighted the Administrative Services department facts and figures on the last page of the
report. She stated that the City's AAA bond rating is unheard of and she expressed pride that the
City ended the fiscal year with $30.1 million in discretionary reserves. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
stated that the annual report is full of good news and she encouraged residents to read it when it
reaches their mail boxes. She further discussed the upcoming Rachel's Challenge program and
the Links of Character element which is meant to start a chain reaction of kind deeds. She
announced that there will be a Rachel's Challenge presentation, hosted by Saddleback College,
on February 8, 2010, at noon. She also recognized that many Mission Viejo schools will
participate in the kindness chain which will culminate at the City’s Arts Alive event on Sunday,
April 25. She stated that the goal is a five-mile chain of kindness. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
reminded residents to vote in the election tomorrow and she shared her contact information for
those who have questions about the issues. She encouraged residents to do their research and

City Council Minutes  7  February 1, 2010
 educate themselves before they vote. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley concluded her comments by
highlighting the Community of Character word for the month of February which is unity.

Mayor MacLean

Mayor MacLean stated that he was offended by Council Member Schlicht’s comments
insinuating that a Deputy Sheriff is in the room because of him. The meetings are video and
audio taped and at no time has he ever treated her with anything but utter professionalism and
kindness. He said that he has allowed her to speak and has never made any threatening remarks,
but he did remind her to turn on her microphone when she frequently forgot. He stated that there
has been an officer in the room as a Sergeant of Arms since 1988 and that it is simply protocol.
Mayor MacLean discussed the recall effort and stated that while he is the subject of the recall, he
is not. He stated that he has been nothing but a vehicle in the means to achieve a power grab and
to change the policies in the City. He asked residents to think about their comfort level with the
quality of life in Mission Viejo. Are they happy with the City’s financial condition, programs
and services and the overall quality of life and if so, he encouraged them to vote no on the recall.
Mayor MacLean stated that regardless of what happens twenty-four hours from now, he will be
at peace and he will have closure. He will have the support of his family and he will be
completely content in knowing that he has served this community with integrity, honor and
honesty. Mayor MacLean stated that he has made an effort to make a difference yet his
opponents won’t have any peace. While they may be able to steal the election, they will also
have the District Attorney nipping at their heels for illegal election activities, possible
prosecution for the evasion of paying taxes for vehicle license fees, and possible fines by the
FPPC for illegal campaign reporting. Mayor MacLean announced that he will close tonight’s
meeting in memory of resident Paul Shepard.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 8:21 p.m., Mayor MacLean recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 8:40 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council considered the final part of the review of
the City Manager. They thoroughly considered the proposed 6th Amendment to the City
Manager's contract and came to a consensus regarding their position on the contract. Mr. Curley
recommended that the Council now address item 7 and treat it as a regular agenda item.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)

7.  Sixth Amendment to City Manager Employment Agreement

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  postpone this item until after the February 2, 2010, election.

City Council Minutes  8  February 1, 2010
   On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, MacLean, and Ury
  ABSENT: None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to
  incorporate changes presented by Mr. Wilberg and his attorney and accept them in total.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Ledesma and Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:58 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor MacLean adjourned the meeting in Memory of Paul Shepard to Monday,
February 15, 2010, at 6:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 15, 2010

City Council Minutes  9  February 1, 2010
